This document summarizes result from the joint analysis of Pool-Seq and Ind-Seq samples of *D. suzukii* including *Wolbachia* endosymbionts together with *D. subpulchrella* and *D. similans* samples representative of outgroup species as detailed in Table @tbl-detsample. These include 12 newly sequenced *D. suzukii* lines.

```{r detsample}
#| echo: false
#| tbl-cap: "Details on the Whole-Genome Sequence samples selected for the study. Sequencing data descriptors were estimated using *fastp* [v0.23.4, @ChenFastp2018] ran with default option."
#| tbl-cap-location: bottom
#| tbl-colwidths: false
#| label: tbl-detsample
tmp=det.sample[,1:7]
tmp$`Seq. Type`=paste0(tmp$`Seq. Type`," (",det.sample$SeqType,")")
tmp$Ref[grepl("Olaz",tmp$Ref)]="@olazcuaga_whole-genome_2020"
tmp$Ref[grepl("Omet",tmp$Ref)]="@ometto_linking_2013"
tmp$Ref[grepl("Camu",tmp$Ref)]="@Camus2024"
tmp$Ref[grepl("Lew",tmp$Ref)]="@lewald_population_2021"
tmp$Ref[grepl("Tur",tmp$Ref)]="@Turelli2018"
tmp$`Nb. reads`=format(det.sample$`TotReadsInit (M)`*1e6,big.mark=",")
tmp$`%GC`=format(det.sample$`%GCInit`,digits=3)
tmp$`%Dup`=format(det.sample$PercentDup,digits=2)
tmp$`%Overlap`=format(100-det.sample$PercentNonOverlap,digits=2)
kable(tmp,align="llcccll")
rm(tmp)
```

# Mapping onto the *IsoJap1* chromosome-level assembly

WGS data were first filtered using *fastp* [v0.23.2; @ChenFastp2018] run with default options to remove contaminating adapter sequences and trim for poor quality bases (i.e., with a phred quality score $<$15). Read pairs with either one read containing more than 40% low-quality bases or more than 5 N bases were removed. The filtered reads were then mapped onto the new chromosome-level IsoJap1 assembly [@Camus2024], complemented with the complete mitochondrial sequence of *D. suzukii* (GenBank Accession ID: *KU588141*) and the complete sequence for the Wolbachia endosymbiont (wRI strain) of *D. simulans* (NCBI ID: *GCA\_000022285*), a Wolbachia strain closely related to that of *D. suzukii* one [@Turelli2018], using the default options of *bwa-mem2* [v2.2.1; @Vasimuddin2019]. PCR duplicates were further removed using the *view* and *markdup* programs of *SAMtools* [v1.19; @LiSamtools2009]. The mean realized coverage was finally estimated using *mosdepth* [v0.3.6; @Pedersen2018] with the option *-Q 20* to ignore reads with low mapping quality. 

## Realized coverage

Mean coverages were estimated  with *mosdepth* [v0.3.6; @Pedersen2018] using the *bam* files obtained from the mapping of the filtered raw reads on the new IsoJap1 chromosome-level assembly [@Camus2024] complemented with the complete mitochondrial sequence of *D. suzukii* (GenBank Accession ID: *KU588141*) and the complete sequence for the Wolbachia endosymbiont (wRI strain) of *D. simulans* (NCBI ID: *GCA\_000022285*); for the i) Wolbachia (W), ii) autosomes (A) consisting of chr2L, chr2R, chr3, and chr4 chromosomes; iii) X-chromosome; and iv) the Mitochondria (M)."

```{r detsample}
colnames(tmp)[-1:-3]=gsub("cov","",colnames(tmp)[-1:-3]) 
for(i in 4:8){tmp[,i]=round(tmp[,i],digits = 2)}

```

## wRI sequence coverage

The variation of coverage for the different individual was estimated with *samtools* using the following command:

```{bash}
#| eval: false
for ii in *.bam
do
samtools view -f 0x2 -O BAM $ii wRI |samtools depth - > $ii.wRI.depth 
done
```

and plotted per consecutive windows of 1 kb for all samples


# Estimation of nucleotide diversity on isofemale lines and comparison with other Pool-Seq samples

Standard nucleotide diversity statistics were first directly estimated from each *bam* file of the 20 Pool-Seq samples (Table @tbl-detsample), for non-overlapping windows (10 kb, 50 kb or 100 kb) over the whole genome, using the estimators for Pool-Seq data developed by @Ferretti2013. Only positions covered by at least two reads and less than 250 reads with a min quality > 20 were considered in the computations (*-mincov 2 -maxcov 250 -minqual 20* options) and windows with less than 9,000 remaining positions were discarded. 

```{r nucdiv}
#| fig-height: 16 
#| fig-width: 16 
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of the estimated nucleotide diversity ($\\theta_\\pi$) for the different chromosomes. Nucleotide diversity was estimated for non-overlapping 50 kb windows using the estimators for Pool-Seq data implemented in *npstat* [@Ferretti2013]. Windows with less than 25,000 callable sites were discarded from representation."
#| fig-cap-location: bottom
#| label: fig-nucdiv
#| echo: false

chr.list=c("chr2L","chr2R","chr3","chrX")#,"chr4")
pop.list=det.sample$`Sample ID`[det.sample$`Seq. Type`!="IndSeq"]
colony.idx=which(grepl("Col-",pop.list))
iso.idx=which(grepl("Om300",pop.list) | grepl("Iso-",pop.list))
dsub.idx=which(grepl("sub",pop.list))
popsuz.idx=(1:length(pop.list))[-c(iso.idx,colony.idx,dsub.idx)]
col.pool=rep(3,length(pop.list))
col.pool[iso.idx]=4
col.pool[colony.idx]=5
col.pool[dsub.idx]=7

win.length=10000
##recup infos lsous form de liste par scaffold avec conversion position (car mapping sur contigs)
win.det=NULL
dum.mat=matrix(NA,0,length(pop.list))
colnames(dum.mat)=pop.list
all.estim=list(length=dum.mat,read_depth=dum.mat,S=dum.mat,Watterson=dum.mat,Pi=dum.mat,Tajima_D=dum.mat)
for(s in 1:length(chr.list)){
 for(p in 1:length(pop.list)){
   tmp.file=paste0(wd,"/ana_npstat/",pop.list[p],".",chr.list[s],".",win.length,".stats.gz")
   tmp.res=read.table(gzfile(tmp.file),h=T)[,c(2,4,5,6,7,8)]
   if(p==1){
     tmp.win.fin=(1:nrow(tmp.res))*win.length
     tmp.win.deb=tmp.win.fin-win.length+1 
     tmp.win.det=data.frame(ctg=rep(chr.list[s],nrow(tmp.res)),start=tmp.win.deb,end=tmp.win.fin)
     if(is.null(win.det)){win.det=tmp.win.det}else{win.det=rbind(win.det,tmp.win.det)}
      tmp.all.estim=array(0,dim=c(nrow(tmp.res),ncol(tmp.res),length(pop.list)),
                                    dimnames = list(rownames(tmp.res),colnames(tmp.res),pop.list))
       tmp.all.estim[,,p]=as.matrix(tmp.res)
     }else{
      tmp.idx=1:min(nrow(tmp.all.estim),nrow(tmp.res))
      tmp.all.estim[tmp.idx,,p]=as.matrix(tmp.res)[tmp.idx,]
     }
   }
    for(j in names(all.estim)){
      all.estim[[j]]=rbind(all.estim[[j]],tmp.all.estim[,j,])
    }
}

win.na=all.estim$length<9000
tmp.pi=all.estim$Pi ; tmp.pi[win.na]=NA
pi.lim=c(0,max(tmp.pi),na.rm=T)
idx.plot=c(dsub.idx,iso.idx,colony.idx,popsuz.idx)

layout(matrix(1:4,2,2))
for(s in 1:length(chr.list)){
vioplot(tmp.pi[win.det$ctg==chr.list[s],idx.plot],col=col.pool[idx.plot],las=2,
        ylab=expression(theta[pi]),main=chr.list[s])
}  

tmp.theta=all.estim$Watterson ; tmp.theta[win.na]=NA
tmp.depth=all.estim$read_depth ; tmp.depth[win.na]=NA
#tmp.S=all.estim$S ; tmp.S[win.na]=NA

nucdiv.sumstats=cbind(paste0(colSums(win.na[win.det$ctg!="chrX",])," (",colSums(win.na[win.det$ctg=="chrX",]),")"),
                      paste0(formatC(apply(tmp.depth[win.det$ctg!="chrX",],2,median,na.rm=T),format="f",digits=1)," (",
                             formatC(apply(tmp.depth[win.det$ctg=="chrX",],2,median,na.rm=T),format="f",digits=1),")"),   
#                      paste0(formatC(apply(tmp.S[win.det$ctg!="chrX",],2,median,na.rm=T),format="f",digits=1)," (",
#                             formatC(apply(tmp.S[win.det$ctg=="chrX",],2,median,na.rm=T),format="f",digits=1),")"),               
                      paste0(formatC(apply(1000*tmp.pi[win.det$ctg!="chrX",],2,median,na.rm=T),format="f",digits=2)," (",
                             formatC(apply(1000*tmp.pi[win.det$ctg=="chrX",],2,median,na.rm=T),format="f",digits=2),")"),
                      paste0(formatC(apply(1000*tmp.theta[win.det$ctg!="chrX",],2,median,na.rm=T),format="f",digits=2)," (",
                             formatC(apply(1000*tmp.theta[win.det$ctg=="chrX",],2,median,na.rm=T),format="f",digits=2),")")
                      )
rownames(nucdiv.sumstats)=colnames(tmp.theta)
```

As expected and shown in Figures @fig-nucdiv and @fig-nucchrdistrib and Table @tbl-nucdiv, all isofemale lines and colonies are depleted in genetic diversity (Figures @fig-nucdiv and @fig-nucchrdistrib) compared to wild population samples.....

# Structuring of genetic diversity

## (Host) autosome on *D. suzukii* samples

Variant calling was performed on the *chr2L*, *chr2R*, *chr3* and *chr4* autosomes using the Haplotype Caller implemented in *FreeBayes* [v1.3.6; @Garrison2012], which does not require realignment around indels and base recalibration, jointly considering all 19 Pool-Seq and 4 Ind-Seq alignment files from *D. suzukii* samples, with the following options *-K -C 1 -F 0.01 -G 5 --limit-coverage 500 -n 4 -m 30 -q 20*. To improve computational efficiency, variant calling was performed in parallel on a computer grid for the 590 non-overlapping 250 kb windows covering the chosen autosomes. The resulting vcf files were reordered and concatenated using the *view* and *concat* programs of *bcftools* [v1.20; @danecek_twelve_2021]. Here is a summary of the raw characteristics of the discovered variants (i.e., before filtration):

```{r sum_autosnp_bef_filt}
#| echo: true
tmp=fread(paste0(wd,"/chr.summary.gz"),h=T,data.table=F)
sort(table(tmp$TYPE),decreasing=T)
#Number of samples with data
summary(tmp$NS)
quantile(tmp$NS,probs=c(0.01,0.05,0.1,0.25,0.75,0.9,0.95,0.99))
#Total read depth at the locus
quantile(tmp$DP[tmp$QUAL>20],probs=c(1e-3,1e-2,1-1e-2,1-1e-3))
#standard filters on
  #QUAL="Quality"
  #SAF="Number of alternate observations on the forward strand"
  #SAR="Number of alternate observations on the reverse strand"
  #RPR="Reads Placed Right: number of reads supporting the alternate balanced to the right (3') of the alternate allele"
  #RPL="Reads Placed Left: number of reads supporting the alternate balanced to the left (5') of the alternate allele"
sum(tmp$QUAL>20 & tmp$SAF > 0 & tmp$SAR > 0 & tmp$RPR > 1 & tmp$RPL > 1)
mean(tmp$QUAL>20 & tmp$SAF > 0 & tmp$SAR > 0 & tmp$RPR > 1 & tmp$RPL > 1)
mean(tmp$QUAL>20 & tmp$SAF > 0 & tmp$SAR > 0 & tmp$RPR > 1 & tmp$RPL > 1 & tmp$DP>100 & tmp$DP<3000)
rm(tmp)
```

Based on these results, the *vcf* was further filtered using a custom *awk* script to keep only bi-allelic variants (including the reference allele) with *QUAL>20, NS>21, 100<DP<3000, SAF>0, SAR>0, RPR>1, RPL>1, EPP>0, SRP>0* and a global MAF computed from the overall read counts >0.01:

```{bash}
#| eval: false
gunzip -c chr*vcf.gz | gawk -f filtersnp.awk -v minns=21 -v maxdp=3000 |gzip -c > auto.filtered.vcf.gz 
```

The resulting filtered *vcf* was analyzed with *poolfstat* utilities.


```{r autopooldata}
hap.size=gsub("[()]","",det.sample$`Haploid Size (X)`)
hap.size=matrix(as.numeric(unlist(strsplit(hap.size," "))),ncol=2,byrow = T)
rownames(hap.size)=det.sample$`Sample ID`
sample.info=hap.size[read.table(paste0(wd,"/res_vcf/sample.ord"))[,1],]
auto.pooldata=vcf2pooldata(vcf.file=paste0(wd,"/auto.filtered.vcf.gz"),poolsizes = sample.info[,1],poolnames = rownames(sample.info))
```


```{r autopca}

scree_data <- data.frame(PC = factor(paste0("PC", 1:length(auto.pca$perc.var)),levels = paste0("PC", 1:length(auto.pca$perc.var))),Variance = auto.pca$perc.var)

tmp4<-ggplot(data, aes(x = PC1, y = PC4, label = sample,color=group)) +
```

## Wolbachia


Variant calling was performed as above on *wRI* Wolbachia sequence using the Haplotype Caller implemented in *FreeBayes* [v1.3.6; @Garrison2012], which does not require realignment around indels and base recalibration, jointly considering all the 27 alignment files from the samples described in Table @tbl-detsample. The following options *-K -C 1 -F 0.01 -G 5 --limit-coverage 500 -n 4 -m 30 -q 20* and the ploidy of the Ind-Seq sample or Pool-Seq samples associated with Iso-female lines or colonies was set to 1.  

Here is a summary of the raw characteristics of the discovered variants (i.e., before filtration):

```{r sum_wRI_bef_filt}
#| echo: true
tmp=fread(paste0(wd,"/wRI.summary.gz"),h=T,data.table=F)
sort(table(tmp$TYPE),decreasing=T)
#Number of samples with data
summary(tmp$NS)
quantile(tmp$NS,probs=c(0.01,0.05,0.1,0.25,0.75,0.9,0.95,0.99))
#Total read depth at the locus
quantile(tmp$DP[tmp$QUAL>20],probs=c(1e-3,1e-2,1-1e-2,1-1e-3))
#standard filters on
  #QUAL="Quality"
  #SAF="Number of alternate observations on the forward strand"
  #SAR="Number of alternate observations on the reverse strand"
  #RPR="Reads Placed Right: number of reads supporting the alternate balanced to the right (3') of the alternate allele"
  #RPL="Reads Placed Left: number of reads supporting the alternate balanced to the left (5') of the alternate allele"
sum(tmp$QUAL>20 & tmp$SAF > 0 & tmp$SAR > 0 & tmp$RPR > 1 & tmp$RPL > 1)
sum(tmp$QUAL>20 & tmp$SAF > 0 & tmp$SAR > 0 & tmp$RPR > 1 & tmp$RPL > 1 & tmp$DP>100)
rm(tmp)
```

Based on these results, the *vcf* was further filtered using a custom *awk* script to keep only bi-allelic variants (including the reference allele) with *QUAL>20, NS>21, DP>100, SAF>0, SAR>0, RPR>1, RPL>1, EPP>0, SRP>0* and a global MAF computed from the overall read counts >0.01:

```{bash}
#| eval: false
gunzip -c wRI.vcf.gz | gawk -f filtersnp.awk -v minns=21 -v maxdp=1e8 |gzip -c > wRI.filtered.vcf.gz 
```

The resulting filtered *vcf* was analyzed with *poolfstat* utilities.

```{r wRIpooldata}
all.sample.info=hap.size[read.table(paste0(wd,"/res_vcf/all.sample.ord"))[,1],]
wRI.pooldata=vcf2pooldata(vcf.file=paste0(wd,"/wRI.filtered.vcf.gz"),poolsizes = all.sample.info[,1],poolnames = rownames(all.sample.info))
```

As expected from the presence of a single Wolbachia genotype, the MAF boxplot on the called SNPs shows a reduced genetic diversity in Individual, Iso-female and Colony sample (Figure @fig-wRImaf). Still, some polymorphism is found at some SNPs (this may also be related to coverage heterogeneity)? 

```{r wRImafdistrib}
#| echo: false
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-width: 8 
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of the MAF of called wRI sites on all the samples ."
#| fig-cap-location: bottom
#| label: fig-wRImaf
wRI.maf=0.5-abs(0.5-wRI.pooldata@refallele.readcount/wRI.pooldata@readcoverage)
colnames(wRI.maf)=wRI.pooldata@poolnames
boxplot(wRI.maf,horizontal=T,las=1,xlab="MAF")
```

The random allele PCA (i.e., ignoring called genotype for presumably haploid Wolbachia sample) shows a clear separation of *D. subpulchrella* Wolbachia on the first PC (Figure @fig-wRIpca). *D. simulans* individual are not spearated from other *D. suzukii* in the first four PCs. Is it biological or resulting from bias due to the mapping on *wRI* sequence? 

```{r wRIpca}
#| echo: false
#| fig-height: 16 
#| fig-width: 24 
#| fig-cap: "Random allele PCA of Wolbachia SNPs on all the 27 samples."
#| fig-cap-location: bottom
#| label: fig-wRIpca
#boxplot(auto.pooldata@readcoverage)
wRI.pca=randomallele.pca(wRI.pooldata,plot.pcs = NULL)
pch.type =rep(16,wRI.pooldata@npools) ; pch.type[wRI.pooldata@poolsizes==2]=17
pch.col  = rep(3,wRI.pooldata@npools)
pch.col[which(grepl("Col-",wRI.pooldata@poolnames))]=5
pch.col[which(grepl("Om300",wRI.pooldata@poolnames) | grepl("Iso-",wRI.pooldata@poolnames))]=4
pch.col[which(grepl("sub",wRI.pooldata@poolnames) | grepl("CN-Kun",wRI.pooldata@poolnames))]=8

# Plot the scree plot
tmp1<-ggplot(scree_data, aes(x = PC, y = Variance)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "steelblue") +  # Bar plot for explained variance
  geom_point(size = 2) +  # Add points to show individual PC values
  geom_line(group = 1, color = "black") +  # Line connecting the points
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Scree Plot", x = "Principal Component", y = "Percentage of Explained Variance") +
  ylim(0, max(wRI.pca$perc.var))

data=as.data.frame(wRI.pca$pop.loadings)
colnames(data)=paste0("PC",1:ncol(data))
data$sample=wRI.pooldata@poolnames
data$group=paste0("G",pch.col)
data$group[pch.col==3]="Wild" ; data$group[pch.col==4]="Col" ; data$group[pch.col==5]="Iso"
data$group[pch.col==7]="Dsim" ; data$group[pch.col==8]="Dsuz" 
# Plot using ggplot and ggrepel to avoid overlapping labels
tmp2<-ggplot(data, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, label = sample,color=group)) +
  geom_point(size=1) +  # Plot points for each sample
  geom_text_repel(max.overlaps = Inf) +  # Add sample names without overlapping
  theme_minimal() + 
  labs(x = paste0("PC1 (",round(wRI.pca$perc.var[1],2),"%)"), 
       y = paste0("PC2 (",round(wRI.pca$perc.var[2],2),"%)"), title = "") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(4,7,8,5,3)) 

tmp3<-ggplot(data, aes(x = PC1, y = PC3, label = sample,color=group)) +
  geom_point(size=1) +  # Plot points for each sample
  geom_text_repel(max.overlaps = Inf) +  # Add sample names without overlapping
  theme_minimal() + 
  labs(x = paste0("PC1 (",round(wRI.pca$perc.var[1],2),"%)"), 
       y = paste0("PC3 (",round(wRI.pca$perc.var[3],2),"%)"), title = "") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(4,7,8,5,3)) 

tmp4<-ggplot(data, aes(x = PC1, y = PC4, label = sample,color=group)) +
  geom_point(size=1) +  # Plot points for each sample
  geom_text_repel(max.overlaps = Inf) +  # Add sample names without overlapping
  theme_minimal() + 
  labs(x = paste0("PC1 (",round(wRI.pca$perc.var[1],2),"%)"), 
       y = paste0("PC4 (",round(wRI.pca$perc.var[4],2),"%)"), title = "") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(4,7,8,5,3)) 

grid.arrange(tmp1, tmp2, tmp3, tmp4, ncol = 2)

rm(data)
```

## Mitochondria

Variant calling was performed as above on *wRI* Wolbachia sequence using the Haplotype Caller implemented in *FreeBayes* [v1.3.6; @Garrison2012], which does not require realignment around indels and base recalibration, jointly considering all the 27 alignment files from the samples described in Table @tbl-detsample. The following options *-K -C 1 -F 0.01 -G 5 --limit-coverage 500 -n 4 -m 30 -q 20*.  

Here is a summary of the raw characteristics of the discovered variants (i.e., before filtration):

```{r sum_Mito_bef_filt}
#| echo: true
tmp=fread(paste0(wd,"/Mito.summary.gz"),h=T,data.table=F)
sort(table(tmp$TYPE),decreasing=T)
#Number of samples with data
summary(tmp$NS)
quantile(tmp$NS,probs=c(0.01,0.05,0.1,0.25,0.75,0.9,0.95,0.99))
#Total read depth at the locus
quantile(tmp$DP[tmp$QUAL>20],probs=c(1e-3,1e-2,1-1e-2,1-1e-3))
#standard filters on
  #QUAL="Quality"
  #SAF="Number of alternate observations on the forward strand"
  #SAR="Number of alternate observations on the reverse strand"
  #RPR="Reads Placed Right: number of reads supporting the alternate balanced to the right (3') of the alternate allele"
  #RPL="Reads Placed Left: number of reads supporting the alternate balanced to the left (5') of the alternate allele"
sum(tmp$QUAL>20 & tmp$SAF > 0 & tmp$SAR > 0 & tmp$RPR > 1 & tmp$RPL > 1)
sum(tmp$QUAL>20 & tmp$SAF > 0 & tmp$SAR > 0 & tmp$RPR > 1 & tmp$RPL > 1 & tmp$DP>100)
rm(tmp)
```

Based on these results, the *vcf* was further filtered using a custom *awk* script to keep only bi-allelic variants (including the reference allele) with *QUAL>20, NS>21, DP>100, SAF>0, SAR>0, RPR>1, RPL>1, EPP>0, SRP>0* and a global MAF computed from the overall read counts >0.01:

```{bash}
#| eval: false
gunzip -c Mito.vcf.gz | gawk -f filtersnp.awk -v minns=21 -v maxdp=1e8 |gzip -c > Mito.filtered.vcf.gz 
```

The resulting filtered *vcf* was analyzed with *poolfstat* utilities.

```{r Mitopooldata}
Mito.pooldata=vcf2pooldata(vcf.file=paste0(wd,"/Mito.filtered.vcf.gz"),poolsizes = all.sample.info[,1],poolnames = rownames(all.sample.info))
```

```{r Mitomafdistrib}
#| echo: false
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-width: 8 
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of the MAF of called Mitochondria sites on all the samples ."
#| fig-cap-location: bottom
#| label: fig-Mitomaf
Mito.maf=0.5-abs(0.5-Mito.pooldata@refallele.readcount/Mito.pooldata@readcoverage)
colnames(Mito.maf)=Mito.pooldata@poolnames
boxplot(Mito.maf,horizontal=T,las=1,xlab="MAF")
```
